"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 1920: a diffuse signal with no simple cause.

What it reads: its input direction is almost entirely MLP hidden unit 1920 of layer 15
(weight 0.90 of a unit-length direction, the rest spread thinly over other units). So it is
that one hidden neuron, written into the residual stream by a fixed direction.

What the data show (about 4.2M training positions, measured on the worker):
- Most positions sit near zero: mean about -0.035, spread about 0.4. The first token of a
  document is almost exactly 0.
- No reliable dependence on the current token's identity or class (digits, Han characters,
  punctuation, words), on the previous token, on the position in the document, on whether the
  token repeats earlier text, or on the document as a whole. Out-of-sample token-identity tables
  reach only about 0.02 variance explained.
- Rare large spikes (|activation| above 2 at about 0.2% of positions, up to about 20, both
  signs) carry about a fifth of the variance. They sit on mixed tokens (digits and hyphenated
  line breaks lean negative or positive, but not reliably), so no short rule picks them out.

So the program predicts the typical value everywhere. That scores about 0 variance explained
and leaves the model's output essentially as switching the component off does.
"""

READS = ()

TYPICAL = -0.035  # mean activation over training positions


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, TYPICAL

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 1921: a diffuse, weak feature with no simple reading.

What it does: predicts the component's typical activation. Its activation is about
0.05 on ordinary tokens, and exactly ~0 on the first token of each document (where the
attention has nothing before it). Everything else is predicted as the average.

Why this simple: over sampled activations, the component's value does not track
token identity (a per-token table does worse than the mean on held-out rows), token
class (letters, digits, punctuation, whitespace), position, repeated-context matches
(induction-like copying), or the character mix of the recent window. Each of these
explains under 1% of its variance on held-out rows. So the honest program is a baseline
that gets the level right and the document-start case right, and nothing more.
"""

READS = ()

ORDINARY = 0.051  # mean activation on ordinary tokens
DOC_START = 0.006  # activation on a document's first token (constant in the data)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    ids, docs = prefix.token_ids, prefix.document_ids
    first_of_doc = len(docs) < 2 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]
    return carry, DOC_START if first_of_doc else ORDINARY

"""Layer 15 MLP unit 1922 (the component reads almost only this hidden unit).

What it responds to: verbatim copying of text that already appeared earlier in the same
document. At each token it measures
  run  - how many consecutive tokens, ending here, repeat an earlier stretch of the
         document (capped at 32), and
  seen - how many times this token has already occurred earlier in the document.
The unit goes negative in proportion to run / (1 + seen): strongest while a long span is
being re-copied for the first or second time, weaker where the text is boilerplate that
has been repeated many times. Otherwise it sits slightly below zero.
"""

READS = ()

MAX_RUN = 32
LOOKBACK = 400
BASE = -0.08
SLOPE = -0.95


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    ids = prefix.token_ids
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    if carry is None or (t > 0 and docs[t] != docs[t - 1]):
        carry = {"start": t, "seen": {}}  # a new document: forget earlier text
    start, seen = carry["start"], carry["seen"]
    earlier = seen.get(ids[t], [])  # earlier places this token occurred in the document
    run = 0
    for s in reversed(earlier):
        if t - s > LOOKBACK:
            break
        k = 0
        while k < MAX_RUN and s - k >= start and ids[s - k] == ids[t - k]:
            k += 1  # how far the match extends backwards from s and t
        run = max(run, k)
    seen.setdefault(ids[t], []).append(t)
    return carry, BASE + SLOPE * run / (1 + len(earlier))

"""Predict the typical value of layer 15 MLP down-projection component 1923.

What the component is: one rank-one piece of the MLP down projection in layer 15. It reads
the MLP's hidden units and writes into the residual stream. Its input direction is about
45% hidden unit 1923 of that layer, and the rest is spread over many other units.
Its activation is a weak linear readout of those hidden units. It correlates about 0.4
with unit 1923 alone, and its contribution is a tiny fraction of the site's output.

What this program does: it has no rule that predicts the activation. Over sampled
training text, the activation is centred near -0.02 with spread 0.32, and no
readable feature we tried explains more than about 0.2% of its variance. Those features
were: token class (letters, digits, punctuation, partial UTF-8 bytes), position in the
document, whether the token or bigram already appeared earlier in the document, and
document identity. So the program predicts the typical value at every position.
Switched off or predicted this way, the component changes the model's next-token
predictions by almost nothing, as measured on eval.
"""

READS = ()

TYPICAL_ACTIVATION = -0.017


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """The activation at this position: the component's typical value."""
    return carry, TYPICAL_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, hidden unit 1924: a weak, mostly token-level offset.

This component almost never acts (causal importance ~0 everywhere) and its
activation is a dense, small, noisy signal (mean about -0.03, std about 0.25).
Nearly all of that variation is not explained by anything a reader can name.
The simple account that does any work is a per-token-class offset:

- the end-of-text token that closes each document sits far below zero,
- digit tokens ('0' to '9') sit a little above the average,
- whitespace and newline tokens sit a little below it,
- common function words (and, or, also, is, of, in, was, the, ...) sit below it,
- everything else sits near the overall mean, slightly below zero.

The program predicts those class means and nothing else. It does not model
the context-dependent part of the activation, which is most of it.
"""

READS = ()

END_OF_TEXT = -0.26
DIGIT_MEAN = 0.044
SPACE_MEAN = -0.038
FUNCTION_WORD_MEAN = -0.027
OTHER_MEAN = -0.032

FUNCTION_WORDS = {
    "and", "or", "also", "is", "of", "in", "was", "are", "which", "you",
    "we", "the", "to", "with", "for",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    token = raw.strip()
    if raw == "<|endoftext|>":
        value = END_OF_TEXT
    elif token == "":
        value = SPACE_MEAN
    elif token.isdigit():
        value = DIGIT_MEAN
    elif token.lower() in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        value = FUNCTION_WORD_MEAN
    else:
        value = OTHER_MEAN
    return carry, value

"""Component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:1925 (Qwen3-1.7B, layer 15 MLP).

What it is: one rank-one piece of the MLP down projection. It reads the MLP's hidden
activations through a direction that is dominated by hidden unit 1925 (about 26% of its
squared weight; the rest is spread over thousands of other hidden units), so its
activation is about 0.31 times that unit's value plus many small terms. Unit 1925 alone
explains about 22% of its variance.

What it responds to: no short, nameable concept that we found. Its activation has std
0.30 and is dense, but:
  - the average activation of each token identity explains about 2% of its variance on
    held-out text, and coarse token classes (digits, capitals, CJK, punctuation,
    direction words) about 0.2%;
  - the previous tokens add about 0.5%;
  - position in the document, a token repeating earlier in the row, and the model's own
    entropy or residual norms have no useful relation to it;
  - the model barely uses it: CI never passes 0.1 on 10M tokens and switching it off
    changes the next-token distribution by ~1e-6 nats.

So this program predicts the component's average value at ordinary positions, and 0 at a
document's first token. It explains essentially none of the variance (about 0). A table of
mean activation per token id would add roughly 2% on held-out text, at the cost of a
100k-entry table that names no concept.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.01
"""The component's average activation over ordinary positions."""


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """The activation at this position: silent at a document's first token, else its mean."""
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    starts_document = len(ids) == 1 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]
    if starts_document:
        return carry, 0.0
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Second item of an "X and Y" / "X or Y" coordination.

The component goes negative on the first word after a coordinating conjunction ("and",
"or", and their translations such as "und", "et", "и", "和"), and on the next few words
of that same item, fading within about five words. A determiner right after the
conjunction ("and the", "or a") does not count as a word of its own, so the item's first
noun or adjective gets the strongest value. A plural noun just before the conjunction
makes the effect about 1.5 times stronger. Symbols, digits and punctuation get a small
value. Punctuation, a new clause or a new document ends the item. Everywhere else the
component is near zero.
"""

READS = ()

CONJUNCTIONS = {"and", "or", "und", "et", "y", "e", "o", "oder", "ou", "и", "или", "&", "和", "或", "与"}
DETERMINERS = {"the", "a", "an", "its", "their", "his", "her", "our", "this", "these", "those", "some", "each", "any", "other", "such", "no"}
PUNCTUATION = {",", ".", ";", ":", "!", "?", "(", ")", "\n"}
# activation by place in the item: 0 is its first word, 1 the next, and so on
PROFILE = [-2.3, -1.3, -0.7, -0.4, -0.2]
PLURAL_BOOST = 1.45
SYMBOL_SCALE = 0.2


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    bare = token.strip()
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        carry = None
    if bare in CONJUNCTIONS:
        plural = len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().endswith("s")
        return (0, plural), 0.0
    if carry is None:
        return None, 0.0
    place, plural = carry
    if bare in DETERMINERS and place == 0:
        index = 0
    else:
        index = place
        place += 1
    if index >= len(PROFILE):
        return None, 0.0
    value = PROFILE[index] * (1.0 if bare.isalpha() else SYMBOL_SCALE)
    if plural:
        value *= PLURAL_BOOST
    if bare in PUNCTUATION:
        return None, value
    return (place, plural), value

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 1928: a locative/temporal "in" detector.

The component is large when a preposition meaning "in" (or "on"/"at") opens an adjunct
that says where or when something happened: "was drafted in the first round", "died in
1990", "elections in Turkey", and "dans", "en", "в" in other languages. It is near zero
on most other tokens. It goes negative when " in" opens a clause after a discourse word
("But in that case", "Wait, in", "since in"), and stays near zero when " in" is a fixed
complement of a verb, adjective or noun ("interested in", "involved in", "increase in").
A determiner right after such a preposition ("in the") picks up a weak share of the signal.

The program predicts this from the words alone: an average activation per word class,
looked up on the current token and the one before it, within the same document. It uses
no model and no state beyond those two tokens.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Prepositions meaning "in" (locative or temporal), in English and other languages.
IN_WORDS = {" in", " в", " en", " dans", " im", " nel", " nella", " во", " nei"}

# Prepositions meaning "on" or "at" (or the same role in other languages): weaker.
ON_AT_WORDS = {" on", " at", " IN", " на", " по", " na", " au", " em", " auf", " sur", " bei"}

# Other prepositions that sometimes open a time or place adjunct: weaker still.
OTHER_WORDS = {" In", "In", "in", " under", " during", " within", " upon", " along", " into",
               " при", " w", " у", " à"}  # fmt: skip

IN_VALUE = 6.8
ON_AT_VALUE = 3.0
OTHER_VALUE = 1.5
CLAUSE_OPENER_VALUE = -2.0
DETERMINER_VALUE = 1.0

# Discourse words that, just before " in", make it open a clause, where it goes negative.
CLAUSE_OPENERS = {"But", "but", "However", "however", "Wait", "whereas", "because", "Because",
                  "since", "Since", "So", "so", "Maybe", "maybe", "perhaps"}  # fmt: skip

# Words that take "in" as a fixed complement, so it is not a free time or place adjunct.
FIXED_COMPLEMENT = {"interested", "involved", "engaged", "engage", "participate",
                    "participated", "invest", "invested", "resulted", "result", "resulting",
                    "increase", "increases", "increased", "decrease", "decreases",
                    "decreased", "change", "changes", "changed", "believe", "believed",
                    "specialized", "employed", "involvement", "interest", "role", "ratio",
                    "variables", "used", "use", "applied", "dissolved", "mistake", "fell",
                    "rise", "rose", "drop", "difference", "reduction", "reduced"}  # fmt: skip

DETERMINERS = {" the", " a", " an", " his", " her", " their", " its", " my", " your", " our"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """Activation at the newest token, from its word and the word before it."""
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_doc else ""
    value = 0.0
    if token in IN_WORDS:
        value = IN_VALUE
        if before.strip() in CLAUSE_OPENERS:
            value = CLAUSE_OPENER_VALUE
        elif before.strip() in FIXED_COMPLEMENT:
            value = 0.0
    elif token in ON_AT_WORDS:
        value = ON_AT_VALUE
    elif token in OTHER_WORDS:
        value = OTHER_VALUE
    elif token in DETERMINERS and (before in IN_WORDS or before in ON_AT_WORDS):
        value = DETERMINER_VALUE
    return carry, float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 1929, read through its down_proj component, as a token rule.

The component's activation closely follows MLP hidden unit 1929 of layer 15 (correlation
about 0.75 on training rows). It is signed, mostly near zero, and has rare large spikes.
Its spikes depend on context: a token alone explains only a few percent of its variance,
and short local context adds little. This program predicts the spikes that token identity
can name, and a baseline elsewhere:

- a line break made of tabs only (e.g. "\\t\\n"), the largest and most common spike;
- a chat or tool-call end tag (<|im_end|>, </tool_call>, </tool_response>);
- the word "return";
- other whitespace made of tabs (indentation);
- a small constant baseline for every other token.

On eval rows this gives variance explained 0.026 and correlation 0.16. Switched in for the
component, it changes the model's next-token predictions about as much as switching the
component off does (kl_fraction 0.90).
"""

import re

READS = ()

TAB_LINE_BREAK = re.compile(r"[ \t]*\t[ \t]*\n[ \t\n]*")  # tab-indented blank line break
TAB_WHITESPACE = re.compile(r"[ \t]*\t[ \t]*")  # tabs and spaces only
END_TAGS = {"<|im_end|>", "</tool_call>", "</tool_response>"}

# Typical activation on each kind of token, measured on training rows.
TAB_LINE_BREAK_VALUE = 4.6
END_TAG_VALUE = 2.4
RETURN_VALUE = 1.5
TAB_WHITESPACE_VALUE = 0.7
BASELINE = 0.07


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if TAB_LINE_BREAK.fullmatch(tok):
        value = TAB_LINE_BREAK_VALUE
    elif tok in END_TAGS:
        value = END_TAG_VALUE
    elif tok.strip() == "return":
        value = RETURN_VALUE
    elif TAB_WHITESPACE.fullmatch(tok):
        value = TAB_WHITESPACE_VALUE
    else:
        value = BASELINE
    return carry, value

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 1930: a weak, mostly diffuse feature.

What it does, in plain terms: this component's activation sits near zero with a
typical value of about -0.025 and a spread of about 0.3. Its rare large positive
values come mostly from a chat model's own replies that are negating something
("As an AI language model, I do not have ...", "I don't have a ...", "it is not
..."): the activation is raised on the word that falls inside a negated phrase.
Negation in ordinary text, and the large negative values (code, URL paths,
boilerplate), are not captured here.

The program predicts:
  - the typical value -0.025 everywhere;
  - a higher value (about +0.18, the average in the data) on tokens of an
    assistant reply that come within three tokens after a negation word.

Measured on training data, this explains almost none of the variance (the
component is not well described by any concept found here); it is a readable
description of where its strongest positive values occur, not a good predictor.
"""

READS = ()

TYPICAL = -0.025  # the component's typical value
NEGATED_REPLY = 0.18  # its mean inside an assistant reply, within 3 tokens of a negation
NEGATION_WORDS = {"not", "no", "never", "cannot", "nor", "neither", "without", "n't", "'t", "nt"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    new_document = (
        carry is None
        or len(prefix.document_ids) < 2
        or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    )
    if new_document:
        carry = {"in_reply": False, "after_start": False, "since_negation": 99}
    # Is the current token inside an assistant turn? Turns start "<|im_start|>assistant".
    if token == "<|im_start|>":
        carry["after_start"] = True
    elif carry["after_start"]:
        carry["in_reply"] = token == "assistant"
        carry["after_start"] = False
    if token == "<|im_end|>":
        carry["in_reply"] = False
    # Value uses the negation's distance from the previous tokens only.
    value = TYPICAL
    if carry["in_reply"] and carry["since_negation"] <= 3:
        value = NEGATED_REPLY
    carry["since_negation"] = 1 if token in NEGATION_WORDS else min(carry["since_negation"] + 1, 99)
    return carry, value

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 1931 (this component's input direction is almost exactly that unit).

A weak, cue-based guess. The unit is sparse and heavy-tailed: mostly near 0, with rare spikes
of either sign (up to about +/-30) inside capitalized names and comment sign-offs. Its sign is
not set by the current token, the previous token, character classes, position in the document,
or whether the text repeats, and those together explain under 1% of its variance.

This program only records the two clearest tendencies:
  * right after a signature dash ("–", "—", "•"), where a username is about to begin, it leans
    positive;
  * right after a naming cue ("Dr", "Mr", "named", "called", ...), where a person's name is
    about to begin, it leans negative.
Everywhere else it predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

SIGNATURE_DASHES = {"–", "—", "•"}
NAME_CUES = {"Dr", "Mr", "Mrs", "Ms", "named", "called", "Director"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return carry, 0.0
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()
    if before in SIGNATURE_DASHES:
        return carry, 0.8
    if before in NAME_CUES:
        return carry, -1.0
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 1932, as the component's activation.

It fires when a new variable is bound inside a block of source code: on the name in a
declaration (`const ctx`, `int n`), in a loop header (`for (int i`, `for x in`) or a
parameter list (`def f(self, player`), on the `=` that binds it, and on the `;` or `)`
that closes that statement. Strongest inside code blocks and loop headers; near zero in
prose.
"""
import re

READS = ()

KEYWORD = r"(?:const|let|var|val|final|auto)"
PRIM = r"(?:int|long|short|char|float|double|bool|boolean|byte|String)"
NAME_NEXT = re.compile(r"(?:\b%s|\b%s)\s*$" % (KEYWORD, PRIM))
DECL_EQ = re.compile(r"(?:\b%s|\b%s)\s+\w+\s*$" % (KEYWORD, PRIM))
PLAIN_LHS = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_]\w*\s*$")
FOR_HEAD = re.compile(r"(?:\bfor\s*\(|^\s*for)\s*$")
DEF_PARAMS = re.compile(r"\bdef\s+\w+\s*\([^)]*$")
END = re.compile(r"[);]+\n?|\)?\n")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc:
        line, depth = carry[1], carry[2]
    else:
        line, depth = "", 0
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    block = 1.0 if depth > 0 or line[:1] in (" ", "\t") else 0.3
    depth += tok.count("{") - tok.count("}")
    before = line[-200:]
    word = tok.strip()
    if word == "=":
        value = 4.0 if DECL_EQ.search(before) else 1.0 if PLAIN_LHS.search(before) else 0.5
    elif word == ":=":
        value = 2.5
    elif re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z_]\w*", word):
        if re.search(r"\bfor\s*\(\s*%s\s*$" % PRIM, before):
            value = 5.0
        elif NAME_NEXT.search(before):
            value = 2.0
        elif FOR_HEAD.search(before):
            value = 2.0
        elif DEF_PARAMS.search(before):
            value = 1.5
        else:
            value = 0.0
    elif END.fullmatch(tok) or re.fullmatch(r"[);]+", word):
        value = 2.0 if DECL_EQ.search(before) else 1.0 if "=" in before else 0.0
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (doc, (before + tok).split("\n")[-1], max(depth, 0)), value * block

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 1933: a near-inert direction. Its activation is mostly
diffuse, context-dependent noise (std 0.3 around about -0.05), with no readable trigger.
The one visible pattern: it dips negative on connectives that set up a contrast or an
alternative ("whereas", "elif", "but", "however", "while", "although", "unlike", "except",
"else", "otherwise", and Chinese 但, 而, 然而). The strongest dips are on "whereas" and
"elif" (mean about -1.2). Everywhere else it sits at its typical value, about -0.05.
A document's first token is ~0.

The program reads only the newest token, so it is stateless.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

TYPICAL = -0.05
STRONG_CONTRAST = {"whereas", "elif", "然而"}
CONTRAST = {"but", "however", "while", "although", "unlike", "except", "else", "otherwise", "但", "而"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    if prefix.position == 0:
        return carry, 0.0
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    if word in STRONG_CONTRAST:
        return carry, -1.2
    if word in CONTRAST:
        return carry, -0.15
    return carry, TYPICAL

"""Predicts the component's typical activation: a constant near its average, except at the
first token of each document, where the component is silent.

The component (layer 15, MLP down-projection, component 1934) reads the layer's MLP hidden
units and has a weak, context-dependent output. Its activation is not predictable from the
current token, its character class, its neighbours or simple repetition features; the best
simple guess is its mean, about -0.07.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN = -0.07  # its average activation over ordinary positions


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # A new document starts here: the component's activation is about zero on its first token.
    first = len(prefix.document_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    return carry, 0.0 if first else MEAN

"""A near-inert MLP unit in layer 15 (hidden unit 1936 of the MLP's down projection).

What the unit does: its activation is almost entirely MLP hidden unit 1936 (its input
weight on that unit is 0.67 of a norm of 0.90), so it writes a small signal into the
residual stream whose size and sign depend on the surrounding text, not on any one token.
Switching it off barely changes the model's next-token predictions.

What this program says, in plain terms:
  * It is silent (about 0) on the first token of each document: the unit does not fire
    at a document's start.
  * It dips negative on sequence and consequence connectives that open a clause about
    what happens next or after something: "consequence", "accordingly", "thus",
    "until", "after", "once", "without", "result", and their Chinese counterparts
    ("之后", "以后", "后", "结果", "因此", "之前", "完").
  * Everywhere else it sits at its usual small positive level (about 0.035).

What this does not capture: most of the variance. Token identity, the previous token,
script, repetition and position explain almost none of the activation (held-out R^2
around 0.001-0.005 for each), so the large positive and negative swings elsewhere are not
described here. A full lookup table of per-token means would not do much better; the
signal is in the surrounding context.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Sequence and consequence connectives: words that introduce what follows as a result,
# or a later point in time.
CONNECTIVES = {
    "consequence", "consequently", "accordingly", "thus", "otherwise", "result",
    "thereafter", "subsequently", "eventually", "until", "after", "once", "without",
    "regardless", "soon",
    "之后", "以后", "后", "结果", "因此", "之前", "完",
}
CONNECTIVE_VALUE = -0.2  # typical level on these words in the data
TYPICAL = 0.035  # the unit's usual small positive level
DOCUMENT_START = 0.0  # silent on a document's first token


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    if len(ids) == 1 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]:
        return carry, DOCUMENT_START
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if word in CONNECTIVES:
        return carry, CONNECTIVE_VALUE
    return carry, TYPICAL

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 1937 (its down_proj component).

What it is: this component reads the MLP hidden unit 1937 of layer 15 (that unit alone
accounts for about 44% of its variance). The activation is mostly near zero, with a heavy
negative tail: about 5% of tokens fall below -3, and those carry most of its variance.

What this program predicts: a negative value on tokens that continue a word or a number

explains only a small part of the variance.

    r"educated at|record label|->|\|"

What it does: the component fires on a "0" that extends a round number such as
10, 100, 1,000 or 100,000. It is strongest when the number is a quantity in
running prose or maths ("the top 100", "per 10,000", "nearest 10"), weaker after an
ordinary word, and weakest after a symbol or in code and tables. It also fires on magnitude words (thousand,
million, hundred, ...), and a little on other zeros inside numbers. Everywhere
else it predicts about zero.

The program reads only the prefix. It rebuilds the number being typed at the
newest token (digits and thousands commas, within the same document) and looks
at the word or symbol just before that number. The values are mean activations
measured on training rows for each case, not fitted to the eval rows.

READS = ()

MAGNITUDE_WORDS = {"hundred", "hundreds", "thousand", "thousands", "million", "billion"}
QUANTITY_WORDS = {"top", "than", "nearest", "per", "over", "under", "fewer", "least", "most",
                  "about", "to", "of", "rounded", "approximately", "up", "around"}

# Mean activation of a round-number "0", by its zero count (1: 10, 2: 100, 3+: 1,000 and up)
# and the kind of word before the number: quantity word, other word, or symbol.
ROUND_ZERO = {1: (6.2, 3.6, 2.8), 2: (9.8, 6.8, 5.0), 3: (10.0, 10.0, 10.0)}
OTHER_ZERO = (2.2, 1.2, 1.4)  # any other "0" inside a number, by the same kinds of word
MAGNITUDE_VALUE = 2.3


def _number_so_far(prefix):
    """Digits and commas ending at the newest token, within its document.

    Returns the text and the index of the token just before it (-1 if none)."""
    i = len(prefix.token_strings) - 1
    doc = prefix.document_ids[i]
    chars = []
    while i >= 0 and prefix.document_ids[i] == doc:
        s = prefix.token_strings[i]
        if s == "" or not all(c.isdigit() or c == "," for c in s):
            break
        chars.insert(0, s)
        i -= 1
    return "".join(chars), i


def _word_before(prefix, i):
    """The nearest non-space token at or before index `i`, within the newest token's document."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    while i >= 0 and prefix.document_ids[i] == doc and prefix.token_strings[i].strip() == "":
        i -= 1
    return prefix.token_strings[i].strip() if i >= 0 and prefix.document_ids[i] == doc else ""


def _kind(word):
    """0 for a quantity word, 1 for another word, 2 for a symbol or punctuation."""
    if word in QUANTITY_WORDS:
        return 0
    return 1 if word.isalpha() else 2


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    if tok in MAGNITUDE_WORDS:
        return carry, MAGNITUDE_VALUE
    if tok != "0":
        return carry, 0.0
    number, before_index = _number_so_far(prefix)
    digits = number.replace(",", "")
    kind = _kind(_word_before(prefix, before_index))
    if len(digits) >= 2 and digits[0] == "1" and set(digits[1:]) == {"0"}:
        zeros = min(len(digits) - 1, 3)  # 10 -> 1, 100 -> 2, 1,000 and up -> 3
        return carry, ROUND_ZERO[zeros][kind]
    return carry, OTHER_ZERO[kind]

LEADER_STAR = -3.0
BLOCK_PROSE = -0.4
DOCSTRING = -0.3
XML_DOC = -0.9
COLON = 0.4

# carry: (state, doc_id); state is "" (code), "block", "doc" or "xml".


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    state, doc_id = carry if carry is not None else ("", None)
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc_id:
        state, doc_id = "", prefix.document_ids[-1]
    # the value at this position depends on the state before this token
    if state == "block":
        value = LEADER_STAR if token.strip() == "*" else BLOCK_PROSE
    elif state == "doc":
        value = DOCSTRING
    elif state == "xml":
        value = XML_DOC
    elif token.strip() == ":":
        value = COLON
    else:
        value = 0.0
    # then update the state with this token's text
    if state == "":
        if BLOCK_OPEN in token:
            state = "block"
        elif DOC_QUOTE in token:
            state = "doc"
        elif XML_LINE in token:
            state = "xml"
    elif state == "block" and BLOCK_CLOSE in token:
        state = ""
    elif state == "doc" and DOC_QUOTE in token:
        state = ""
    elif state == "xml" and "\n" in token:
        state = ""
    return (state, doc_id), float(value)

Switching it off barely changes the model (KL ~1e-5 nats per position), so predicting 0

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):

"""Layers.15 MLP hidden unit 1953 (component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:1953).

What the unit is: its rank-one component reads almost only MLP hidden unit 1953 of
layer 15 (about 60% of its input energy; the rest is spread over many units) and writes along the unembedding of words like
"individual(s)", "eligible", "enrol", "recruitment" and "人群" (population).

What it responds to, in plain terms: words that name the people a text is about in
health, medical and social research ("patients", "participants", "students", "young",
"residents", "veterans", "cohort", "population"), and disease or study terms ("HIV",
"diabetes", "disease", "risk", "clinical", "screening", "study"). It is highest on the
noun itself, and a little raised on the connecting word ("for", "among", "with", "to")
that follows such a term within a few tokens.

What this program does: it predicts that activation from the words seen so far.
Each position gets a base value; a population word or a disease/study word on the
current token adds a large amount; a population or disease word in the few tokens before
adds a smaller amount, more so if the current token is a connecting word. It only reads
the current document's tokens, so documents do not leak into each other.

What it misses: most of the component's variance is not word-driven. Neither the
current token nor the previous one explains more than about 1% of its variance, and the
bulk of its values (roughly -1 to +1 on common words) is context noise this program does
not model. So the program captures the large positive spikes on these words, and
predicts a near-zero baseline everywhere else.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Nouns for the people a health or social text is about.
POPULATION = frozenset(
    """patients patient participants participant people individuals individual adults adult
    children child young youth older students student residents resident women veterans
    veteran population populations group groups cohort subjects sample users families
    workers prisoners alumni""".split()
)

# Disease, health-care and study terms.
HEALTH_STUDY = frozenset(
    """hiv aids diabetes disease diseases illness infection obesity overweight mortality
    risk clinical treatment screening health medical hospital hospitalized study randomized
    eligible recruited incarceration prison""".split()
)

# Words that tend to introduce such a group ("for vulnerable...", "among the groups").
CONNECTORS = frozenset("for among with to of by in and from at on after".split())

BASE = 0.075
TOPIC_NOW = 1.4  # population noun on the current token
HEALTH_NOW = 1.6  # disease or study term on the current token
TOPIC_BEFORE = 0.27  # such a term within the 5 tokens before, same document
CONNECTOR_BOOST = 0.17  # a connecting word, after such a term


def _word(text: str) -> str:
    return text.strip().lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    words = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    current = _word(words[-1])
    value = BASE
    if current in POPULATION:
        value += TOPIC_NOW
    if current in HEALTH_STUDY:
        value += HEALTH_NOW
    # Look back at most 5 tokens, stopping at the document boundary.
    topical_before = False
    for i in range(len(words) - 2, max(-1, len(words) - 7), -1):
        if docs[i] != docs[-1]:
            break
        if _word(words[i]) in POPULATION or _word(words[i]) in HEALTH_STUDY:
            topical_before = True
            break
    if topical_before:
        value += TOPIC_BEFORE
        if current in CONNECTORS:
            value += CONNECTOR_BOOST
    return carry, float(value)

a WordNet noun) that completes a multi-word noun phrase, the head in "reproduction [rate]",
"calibration [process]", "drainage [system]", "retention [ability]".

- 0 unless the token is a whole-word noun inside the same document, not its first token.
- +0.4 if the word before is a content word (a word that is not a determiner, preposition,
  conjunction or auxiliary).
- +1.0 more if the word before is a nominalisation (-tion, -sion, -ment, -ance, -ence,
  -ity, -ism), as in "calibration process".
- +1.5 if the head is a method, procedure or system noun (by WordNet hypernym), or one of
  a short list of generic technical head nouns (system, rate, process, layer, signal,
  device, ...), wherever it sits in the phrase.

Near zero on function words, verbs, word fragments and most other tokens. It explains about
5% of the component's variance; a full token table would explain more, but needs thousands
of entries.
"""

from functools import lru_cache

import wordnet

READS = ()

FUNCTION_WORDS = frozenset(
    "a an the this that these those its their his her our your my of in on at for with from "
    "by to into as and or but than is are was were be been has have had it not".split()
)
NOMINALISATION = re.compile(r"(tion|sion|ment|ance|ence|ity|ism)$")


TECHNICAL_HEADS = frozenset(
    "system systems process processes method methods model models function functions device "
    "devices rate rates file files mode modes layer layers region regions unit units cell cells "
    "signal signals matrix program programs algorithm mechanism procedure technique area areas "
    "period plan tool problem scheme buffer site sites effect effects phase platform circuit".split()
)


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def is_noun(word):
    return "noun" in wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def is_way_of_working(word):
    """Method, procedure or system nouns, by WordNet hypernym."""
    return any(wordnet.is_a(word, kind) for kind in ("method", "procedure", "system"))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = cur.strip().lower()
    if prefix.position == 0 or cur[:1] != " " or not word.isascii() or not word.isalpha():
        return carry, 0.0
    if prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1] or not is_noun(word):
        return carry, 0.0

    value = 0.0
    if before.isalpha() and before not in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        value += 0.4
    if NOMINALISATION.search(before):

    if is_way_of_working(word) or word in TECHNICAL_HEADS:
        value += 1.5
    return carry, value

"""Layer 15 MLP, hidden unit 1955: the component's output is mostly that unit's value.

The unit is a gated MLP unit, value = silu(gate) * up. Its gate opens almost only on names
inside source code, above all the names in import lines: the class name at the end of
`import org.graviton.utils.Utils;` (or a `.Utils` piece of it) is where it goes most negative,
because its up-projection is negative there. Lowercase package names in an import line are
mildly negative. Outside import lines it is weakly negative on capitalised names (class names)
in code-dense text, and near zero in prose.

This program predicts that: a strong negative value on class names in import lines, a weaker
one on package names there, a weak negative on capitalised names in dense code, zero elsewhere.
It gets the sign and the places right but explains only about 0.6% of the variance on eval
(r about 0.10): the gate is not readable from the surface text, so most of the variance is
unexplained, and positive values in prose are not modelled.
"""
import re

READS = ()

NAME = re.compile(r"\.?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")
CLASS_NAME = re.compile(r"\.?[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*")
IMPORT_LINE = ("import ", "from ", "using ", "use ", "#include")
IMPORT_VALUE = -2.5  # names in an import line: class names most of all
PACKAGE_VALUE = -1.0  # lowercase package names in an import line
CODE_NAME_VALUE = -0.5  # capitalised names in dense code
DENSE = 0.4  # share of recent tokens that look like code


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    line, code_share = carry if carry else ("", 0.0)
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        line, code_share = "", 0.0
    line = tok.split("\n")[-1] if "\n" in tok else line + tok
    # code-like tokens continue a word with no leading space, or are punctuation
    codey = not tok.startswith(" ") and tok.strip() != "" and not tok.strip().isdigit()
    code_share = 0.95 * code_share + 0.05 * codey
    name = tok.strip()
    value = 0.0
    if NAME.fullmatch(name) and line.lstrip().startswith(IMPORT_LINE):
        value = IMPORT_VALUE if CLASS_NAME.fullmatch(name) else PACKAGE_VALUE
    elif CLASS_NAME.fullmatch(name) and not tok.startswith(" ") and code_share > DENSE:
        value = CODE_NAME_VALUE
    return (line, code_share), value

What it does: its activation is strongly negative on plural nouns (numbers, lines,
equations, digits, children, eyes) and moderately negative on the plural words
"are", "were", "they" and "them". Other tokens sit near zero. The program gives each
plural noun a value of -1.0, each of those four plural words -0.8, and every other
token 0.

singular form (from `inflect`) must be a noun in WordNet, and the word itself must be
a noun in WordNet. This catches regular and irregular plurals (children, teeth, people)
and skips verbs like "is" and "has".

the activation ranges from about -16 to +2, and the strongest negatives are not
predictable from the word alone. Most of the variance comes from ordinary tokens
with no lexical pattern.

import wordnet

PLURAL_PRONOUNS = {"are", "were", "they", "them"}


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def is_plural_noun(word):
    """True for a plural noun: `word` ends in s, its singular is a WordNet noun."""
    if len(word) < 4 or not word.isalpha() or not word.endswith("s"):
        return False

    if is_plural_noun(word):

        return carry, -0.8
    return carry, 0.0

"""Clause-break detector for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 1977.

The component goes negative where prose is joined into a run of semicolon-separated
clauses. It is most negative on the conjunction that opens the clause after a semicolon
("...fiscal year; [and] ..."), and negative on the semicolon itself (strongest for the
full-width "；"). Other words after a semicolon are mildly negative, and " and" right after
a comma (joining clauses or list items) is weakly negative. Everything else is 0.
Values are the mean activation in each class on training text.
"""

READS = ()

SEMICOLONS = {";", ".;", " ;", ");", "；"}
FULLWIDTH_SEMICOLON = -13.7
SEMICOLON = -6.3
AND_AFTER_SEMICOLON = -16.9
OTHER_OPENER = -9.0            # but, or, et, however, that, the, ... after a semicolon
OPENERS = {" But", " but", " or", " And", " et", " however", " that", " the"}
WORD_AFTER_SEMICOLON = -2.3    # any other word after a semicolon
SPACE_AFTER_SEMICOLON = -4.1   # a space or line break after a semicolon
AND_AFTER_COMMA = -1.3


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_doc else ""
    if cur in SEMICOLONS:
        return carry, FULLWIDTH_SEMICOLON if cur == "；" else SEMICOLON
    if prev in SEMICOLONS:
        if cur == " and":
            return carry, AND_AFTER_SEMICOLON
        if cur in OPENERS:
            return carry, OTHER_OPENER
        if cur.strip().isalpha():
            return carry, WORD_AFTER_SEMICOLON
        if not cur.strip():
            return carry, SPACE_AFTER_SEMICOLON
        return carry, 0.0
    if cur == " and" and prev == ",":
        return carry, AND_AFTER_COMMA
    return carry, 0.0

"""Randomness detector: a sparse, negative signal on words about chance.

When this component's activation is strongly negative, its output pushes the
next-token prediction toward randomness words (its direction, read through the
unembedding, promotes "random", "randomly", "randomness", "unpredictable").
Its large negative values sit on words that name randomness, and on code that
calls a random-number generator (`np.random`, `.rand`, `rng.`, `random.choice`).
Shortly after such a word it stays mildly negative.

The program predicts only this, and 0 everywhere else:
- -8 on a randomness word (random, rand, rng, unpredictable, stochastic),
- -1 on a chance word (chance, dice, coin, lottery, luck, pick, probability, ...),
- a weak echo, -1 on the next token after a randomness word and -0.3 on
  the next few after it, within the same document.

This explains only about 3% of the activation's variance (eval: 0.033, r 0.19).
Most of it is small, spread over all kinds of tokens, and not tied to any word
list, and the component's effect on the model's output is tiny either way.
"""

import re

READS = ()

RANDOM = re.compile(r"(?<![a-z])rand|random|rng|unpredict|stochastic")
CHANCE = {
    "chance", "chances", "dice", "coin", "toss", "flip", "roll", "luck",
    "lottery", "gamble", "odds", "probability", "pick", "picked", "picking",
    "sampled", "sampling", "guess", "noise", "outcome", "shuffle",
}
WINDOW = 5  # tokens after a randomness word that still echo it


def _kind(text):
    word = text.strip().lower()
    if RANDOM.search(word):
        return "random"
    if word in CHANCE:
        return "chance"
    return None


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    value = 0.0
    for back in range(WINDOW + 1):
        i = t - back
        if i < 0 or prefix.document_ids[i] != prefix.document_ids[t]:
            break
        kind = _kind(prefix.token_strings[i])
        if back == 0:
            value += {"random": -8.0, "chance": -1.0}.get(kind, 0.0)
        elif kind == "random":
            value += -1.0 if back == 1 else -0.3
    return carry, value

A weak, lexical guess at what this component does. Its activation is a signed,
dense, mostly context-dependent signal (std about 0.5, with rare large positive

description ("vivid", "remembered", "memories", "imagination", "perception",
"visualize", "familiar", "impression", "descriptions"), and its output direction
pushes the next-token distribution toward the same family of words.

This program does the simple version: each token from that imagery/memory/
perception family adds one to a running score, which decays by half per token
and resets at each document boundary. The prediction is that running score,
scaled down. It captures only a small part of the variance (see the explanation).

READS = ()

# Words about memory, imagining, picturing, perceiving and describing.
IMAGERY = re.compile(
    r"imag|memor|vivid|percep|remember|recall|picture|visual|impress"
    r"|dream|familiar|fantas|mental|photo|descri|heard",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
DECAY = 0.5  # the score halves with each later token
SCALE = 0.5  # roughly the least-squares slope on sampled training rows


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    score, doc = carry if carry is not None else (0.0, None)
    doc_now = prefix.document_ids[-1]

        score = 0.0

    score = DECAY * score + (1.0 if IMAGERY.search(token) else 0.0)
    return (score, doc_now), SCALE * score

"""Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:1983, read as a clause-opener detector.

This component is largely MLP hidden unit 1983 of layer 15: that unit's gate-times-up value,
scaled by about 1.19, accounts for roughly 56% of the component's variance. The rest is
diffuse: no token identity or document-level feature predicts it well, and the rule below
captures under 1% of it.

What the program does, in plain terms:
- Negative on a word that opens a sentence with a time or subordinating adverbial
  ("Once", "After", "Before", "Upon", "Having", "When", "As", "During", "Following",
  "While").
- Positive on the first comma after such an opener, which closes the introductory clause
  ("After the case was pending in Phoenix[,] ..."). Many of the component's largest positive
  values fall on such commas.
- Zero everywhere else.

newline. Values are per-word mean activations measured on training rows.
"""

READS = ()

# Value on a sentence-opening word, by word (lower case).
OPENER = {
    "once": -4.0, "after": -3.0, "before": -2.1, "upon": -1.8, "having": -1.4,
    "when": -0.9, "as": -0.8, "during": -0.8, "following": -0.7, "while": -0.6,
}
# Value on the comma that closes the clause that the opener started, by opener.
CLOSE = {
    "once": 1.7, "after": 1.9, "before": 1.6, "upon": 0.8, "having": 0.6,
    "when": 0.5, "as": 0.5, "during": 0.9, "following": 0.5, "while": 1.0,
}
BOUNDARY = set(".!?\n")
COMMAS = {",", "，"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = tok.strip()
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if carry is None or new_doc:
        start, key = True, None  # at a sentence start; no opener pending
    else:
        start, key = carry
    value = 0.0
    if word:
        if start and word.lower() in OPENER:
            value = OPENER[word.lower()]
            key = word.lower()  # an introductory clause is now open
        elif word in COMMAS and key is not None:
            value = CLOSE[key]
            key = None  # the clause is closed
        start = False
    if any(c in BOUNDARY for c in tok):
        start, key = True, None
    return (start, key), value
